lead: Hillsides with views, summer houses and the Park Güell a short walk away.
text: It began to be developed in the second half of the 19th century around the church of Nostra Senyora de la Salut, when fields and farmhouses (masies) still dominated the area. With the arrival of the trams, in 1880 and 1909, it became a summer retreat for Barcelona's bourgeoisie, and from that period date the Reial Santuari de Sant Josep de la Muntanya, built in 1902, and many houses with real character.

It lies on the southern slopes of El Carmel and La Rovira, which you notice in the climbs and the views. It is a quiet, residential neighbourhood, with Gaudí's Park Güell next to its mountain edge and the Travessera de Dalt as its main axis. Its sale price, 4,487 €/m², sits between that of Vallcarca i els Penitents and that of La Vila de Gràcia.
housing: Summer houses and low-rise buildings, on sloping streets.
places: Reial Santuari de Sant Josep de la Muntanya
